free_tier.stated: "We offer unlimited storage and serving of public repositories". Red Hat's own support article. Every paid plan is priced only by private-repo count and lists 'Unlimited public repos'; a free account gets unlimited public repos, private repos require a 30-day trial then a paid plan.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: Every paid plan is priced only by private-repo count and lists 'Unlimited public repos'; a free account gets unlimited public repos, private repos require a 30-day trial then a paid plan

egress.terms: Included in 'unlimited storage and serving of public repositories'. No per-GB line item exists for public repos on any plan. Served over quay.io's own CDN edge.

tooling: oras push / docker push / skopeo; standard distribution-spec v2 registry (Docker-Distribution-API-Version: registry/2.0). Cosign/notation signing supported natively.
chaining: N public repos x N free Red Hat accounts. Repos are namespaced per user/org, so one account already gives effectively unbounded blob count; orgs are free to create.
limits_note: Requires a Red Hat SSO account to push (anonymous pull only). Quay is a shared hosted registry: pull QPS and total storage are subject to undisclosed fair use; the paid tiers exist purely to buy private repos, which signals public storage is deliberately not metered.
